skills.name: Council of High Intelligence
skills.summary: 18 thinker personas (Feynman, Taleb, Munger, Torvalds, Socrates and more) deliberate a hard decision. They analyse blind first, cross-examine each other anonymously, then vote. A chairman writes the verdict, including what would prove it wrong and one concrete next step.

spend.idle: ~650 tokens per session (the 18 agent descriptions). The skill itself loads only when you call it.
spend.perUse: --quick or --duo: ~50–90k tokens. Default (3 personas): ~120–250k. --full (all 18): ~1–1.5M, about 100× a normal answer.

bestFor: Decisions that are expensive to reverse: pricing, architecture, launch plans
"Should multi-person splitting be free or Pro?"-type product calls
Stress-testing a plan you're already leaning towards
avoid: Coding tasks, factual lookups, anything a test can answer
Questions already decided
--full: going from 3 to 18 personas costs a lot and adds little
howTo: /council --quick <question>   → cheapest real deliberation
/council --duo <question>     → two opposing personas
/council <question>           → default 3-persona panel, 3 rounds
/council --triad strategy <question>   → pick the panel
On the laptop add --no-auto-route to keep seats off your local Ollama model
skills.notes: Local patches: runs only when you type /council; Codex seats are read-only; personas can't run shell commands. See skills/council/LOCAL_PATCHES.md.

skills.name: REA: Reverse Engineer Anything
skills.summary: Inspects shipped apps without their source code: native binaries, Electron/JavaScript apps, .NET, Android, firmware and websites. It explains how a feature works, with the evidence and limits behind each conclusion. Analysis runs locally.

spend.idle: ~75 tokens per session (skill description), plus the MCP tool list. That list is large (~180 tools), but Claude Code holds big tool sets back until needed.
spend.perUse: ~6k tokens for the skill and up to ~13k for references when it loads them. Decompiled output can add 20–200k depending on the target.

bestFor: "How does app X implement feature Y?" on software you're allowed to analyse
Checking what's inside your own builds (SplitEven APK/AAB, Electron bundles)
Security review of your own shipped artifacts
avoid: Normal source repos (just read the code)
DRM or licence bypass, cheats, anything a target's terms forbid (see the project's DISCLAIMER)
howTo: Needs Node.js; setup.ps1 registers the 'rea' MCP server pinned to 6.5.0
For native binaries install Ghidra (free); Hopper is macOS-only
"Use REA to analyse how <app> does <feature>"

skills.notes: Responsible-use policy in the upstream DISCLAIMER.md applies.
